perf.summary: Scale does p / scale (3 divides); if the same scale is reused across a march loop the reciprocal could be hoisted by the caller.
perf.currentCost: 3 vector divides per call. In a ray-march, the same scale vector is typically constant for an object, so dividing every evaluation is redundant work.
perf.proposedChange: Offer a companion that takes a precomputed inverse: 'public static float3 Scale(float3 p, float3 invScale) => p * invScale;' or document that callers hoist math.rcp(scale). Keep existing div-based overload for ergonomics.
perf.rationale: Multiply-by-reciprocal hoisted out of the hot loop removes 3 divides per SDF evaluation. Additive API; the existing semantics are unchanged.
perf.risk: Additive overload only; p*rcp(scale) vs p/scale may differ by one ULP. Note rounding caveat if bit-exactness required.

perf.summary: Repeat computes p / cellSize then multiplies cellSize back; uses a divide that becomes mul-by-reciprocal if invCellSize is supplied.
perf.currentCost: 3 divides (p/cellSize) plus round plus mul. The divide is the costly part and is loop-invariant in cellSize across a tiled domain.
perf.proposedChange: Add overload taking invCellSize: 'p - cellSize * math.round(p * invCellSize)'. Caller hoists math.rcp(cellSize) once. Keep current overload.
perf.rationale: Removes 3 divides per evaluation in tiled/instanced SDF scenes where cellSize is constant; replaced by precomputed rcp and muls.
perf.risk: Additive overload; rounding of round(p*invCellSize) vs round(p/cellSize) could land on a different integer exactly at cell boundaries (where p/cellSize is an exact .5). This is a genuine edge-case semantics risk at tile seams — guard by keeping the divide-based version as default and only using the rcp variant where seam exactness is not critical.
